title: Bounding Immersed Curves by Stable Singular Disk Maps
statement: Given a generically immersed closed curve $\gamma$ in an oriented surface $S_g$, does there exist a compact $3$-manifold $M$ with $\partial M=S_g$ and a proper map $D\to M$ from a disk, having only stable singularities, such that $\partial D=D\cap S_g=\gamma$?
background:
Collected from Oberwolfach Reports, which document mathematical workshops and their open-problem discussions.

**Source report:** [Algebraic Structures in Low-Dimensional Topology (2015), Oberwolfach Reports, DOI 10.4171/owr/2014/26, pp. 1403--1458](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2014/26)

## Literature review (checked 2026-08-21)

**Status:** open

**Assessment.** Parity gives obstructions and the free-knot case has substantial partial results, but no general existence criterion for a bounding 3-manifold and stable-singularity disk map for every immersed curve was found.

**Sources checked.**

- [Manturov, Parity and cobordism of free knots](https://doi.org/10.1070/SM2012v203n02ABEH004219)
- [Oberwolfach Report 26, stable-singularity disk problem](https://doi.org/10.4171/owr/2014/26)
